The problem asks for the change in entropy ($\Delta S$) for heating one mole of solid silver from 273 to 333. The provided heat capacity equation in the prompt appears to contain typos (resulting in negative heat capacity values), but it closely resembles the standard form $C_p = 2.5 + 0.023T$ (cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$) often found in thermodynamics problems for this specific temperature range (273 K to 333 K).

Using the standard equation $C_p = 2.5 + 0.023T$ and the range 273 K to 333 K:
$$ \Delta S = \int_{273}^{333} \frac{2.5 + 0.023T}{T} dT = 2.5 \ln\left(\frac{333}{273}\right) + 0.023(333 - 273) $$
$$ \Delta S \approx 2.5(0.1986) + 0.023(60) \approx 0.4965 + 1.38 \approx 1.8765 \text{ eu/mole} $$
Rounding this value gives approximately 1.9 eu/mole. While some sources for this specific problem text cite 1.75, the calculated value is much closer to 1.9, and 1.9 is a provided option.
